bound_selection_uncertain.statement: Triggering is selected by reaching a late turn boundary, so triggered and untriggered cohorts are not randomized or exchangeable; their strict rates cannot identify treatment effect.

failure_cause_unknown.statement: Both other run failures have the coarse class FatalError, but the answer-blind sidecar does not establish their cause or whether G1 introduced them.

g0_g1_descriptive_comparison.statement: The independent G0 baseline had 33 strict passes and six timeout failures over the same frozen 56; G1 had 30 strict passes and zero timeout failures. These are unpaired single-run totals, not causal treatment effects.

g1_bound_outcomes.statement: All five triggered tasks completed; one had a strict-true verdict and four had strict-false verdicts. This is an outcome partition, not a counterfactual effect estimate.

g1_outcome_partition.statement: G1 ended all 56 frozen no-hint tasks: 54 completed, zero 1200-second runner timeouts, two other run failures, 30 strict passes over all 56, and three completed tasks with unknown strict verdicts. Timeouts remain failures in the fixed denominator.

g1_trigger_reach.statement: The answer-blind deadline-reserve event recorded a trigger on five tasks and no trigger on 51; the trigger path was exercised but only a small subset reached it.

g1_unbound_outcomes.statement: Among 51 untriggered tasks, 49 completed and two failed; 29 were strict-true, 17 strict-false, and three had unknown strict verdicts. The two run failures were recorded only as FatalError class, without a cause taxonomy.

nonbinding_not_causal_control.statement: An untriggered G1 task is only an in-run mechanism guard; comparison with a separate stochastic G0 run cannot prove the added policy was inert or isolate a causal effect.

timeout_mechanism_unproven.statement: The evidence does not show which G0 timeout tasks correspond to G1 triggered tasks or whether the changed timeout total arose from the reserve signal rather than run-to-run variation.

timeouts_not_equal_task_gain.statement: The timeout count is lower in G1 while the strict pass count is also lower; a timeout-count change cannot by itself be treated as task-success improvement.

trigger_not_sufficient_for_strict.statement: Four of five triggered G1 tasks completed without a strict pass, so reaching the reserve and submitting within the limit is not sufficient for a strict pass.

unknown_verdicts.statement: Three completed G1 tasks lack a strict verdict. They remain unknown and in the fixed denominator; no validator or answer inspection is permitted to repair the labels.
